reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review contract, assessment rubric, fresh-review framework, resource context, full `SubstanceNucleicAcid` structure report, the deterministic aggregate as prior context, the direct HTTP endpoint finding, and shared Resource/DomainResource behavior context. I also checked the local R4 and R6 package artifacts: R4 has a concrete draft `SubstanceNucleicAcid`; R6 ballot4 has `Substance` and `SubstanceDefinition` but no same-id `SubstanceNucleicAcid` StructureDefinition.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 `SubstanceNucleicAcid` is FMM 0/trial-use, so the burden to preserve a complete legacy resource identity is weak. That lowers the presumption of broad production dependence, but it does not eliminate concern where the removed content is the resource's core scientific/regulatory data or where low-cost R6 guidance could prevent lossy expert-dependent migration.

overall.oneLineConclusion: R6 removes `SubstanceNucleicAcid`, making resource-level migration unavoidable, but low-cost successor mapping and nucleic-acid semantics guidance still have real value.

reasoning.thesisMd: This is not a mostly stable resource with a few local breaks. The R4 concrete resource identity is gone in the R6 ballot package, with the closest local evidence pointing to broader `SubstanceDefinition`/`Substance` modeling. A migration program is therefore unavoidable before R4 instances can be accepted by R6 validators, SDKs, or REST routing. However, accepting the resource redesign does not make all compatibility work pointless: the most valuable remaining standards work is not preserving every old path, but making the successor mapping explicit enough to avoid loss of computable nucleic-acid structure and interpretation rules.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The actual migration shape is removed/replaced-resource plus non-mechanical content mapping. R4 instances with `resourceType: "SubstanceNucleicAcid"` are old-valid/new-invalid in R6 because no same-name StructureDefinition exists. The R4 model carried specialized optional fields for sequence type, subunit count, hybridisation, oligonucleotide type, subunits, sequence attachments, terminal residues, linkages, sugars, identifiers, and residue sites. R6 `SubstanceDefinition` has general classification and structure representation fields, but those are not a same-path or obviously lossless replacement. Real migration needs a policy choice about target resource, representation format, extensions/profile, and round-trip expectations.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: A full deprecated R6 `SubstanceNucleicAcid` resource or legacy REST endpoint would preserve the most wire compatibility, but for FMM 0/trial-use content it would also keep duplicate substance identities, generated types, routes, profile bases, and ambiguity about whether the specialized or generic substance model is authoritative. That makes full legacy preservation relatively low leverage once the resource-removal decision is accepted. The higher-leverage compatibility work is low-cost preservation where possible: explicit successor documentation, transition guidance in CapabilityStatement or migration notes, and nucleic-acid-specific interpretation guidance in or around `SubstanceDefinition.structure`.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The broad less-breaking base option is to retain `SubstanceNucleicAcid` as deprecated for a transition release; that would preserve R4 resourceType, generated code, and endpoint shape but has substantial model-duplication cost. A more targeted option is to add governed optional nucleic-acid structure/profile/extension guidance under `SubstanceDefinition`, especially for subunit/linkage/sugar details and 5'-3' assumptions. A ConceptMap or StructureMap alone is not a less-breaking base design, but an authoritative conversion map is still necessary migration infrastructure because the old structured fields otherwise become expert-dependent text/document mappings.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The direct behavior finding is the base CapabilityStatement endpoint inventory: `SubstanceNucleicAcid` is among the R4 endpoints no longer advertised. For this resource, that is a derivative effect of the missing R6 resource identity rather than an independent data-model break. Generic clients and conformance tooling can still be affected, so replacement documentation or explicit endpoint-removal notes are useful, but standard alias endpoint support would effectively require retaining the removed resource model. Shared `Resource` and `DomainResource` operation/search behavior findings were considered only as global context and were not used to score this resource.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I agree with the deterministic aggregate that major migration is unavoidable and that the migration shape is `removed-or-replaced-resource`. I do not fully adopt its `migration-program-dominates` posture, because the structure findings show specific low-cost or moderate-cost preservation work that still matters after the resource removal: especially explicit successor mapping and semantic guidance for nucleic-acid structure. The right posture is therefore migration expected, but preserve compatibility and meaning where low-cost.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: The same-id R6 resource absence is high-confidence. The precise intended successor is less certain because the local inputs did not include an official HL7 cross-version diff, migration guide, ConceptMap, or StructureMap, and the R6 input is a ballot package rather than a final publication.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 removes the concrete SubstanceNucleicAcid resource identity
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the decisive resource-level break: every R4 instance naming `SubstanceNucleicAcid` lacks a same-id R6 StructureDefinition, and generated validators/clients cannot treat it as a native R6 resource. Because the artifact was FMM 0/trial-use, this does not by itself justify restoring the legacy resource, but it does make a resource-level migration program unavoidable.

findingConsiderations.title: R4 nucleic-acid-specific fields have no same-path R6 content model
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This finding remains standards-review-worthy despite the broader removal. The affected fields are the core scientific/regulatory content of the resource, and mapping them into generic `SubstanceDefinition.structure.representation`, documents, or local extensions can lose computable subunit, linkage, sugar, sequence, and residue-site meaning unless the base specification supplies a governed bridge.

findingConsiderations.title: Generated R6 code and REST dispatch will not contain SubstanceNucleicAcid
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The runtime/codegen break is real for adopters, but it is the predictable application-surface consequence of the accepted resource identity removal. Once the resource redesign is accepted, restoring a generated class, validator entry, search surface, and route would require retaining a deprecated resource model, which is relatively high-cost for FMM 0 content.

findingConsiderations.title: Nucleic-acid-specific conformance semantics are no longer expressed as a resource contract
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is not an additional hard validation break beyond resource removal, but it is a low-cost-to-preserve concern. R4 supplied interpretation rules for 5'-3' direction, omitted subunit count, subunit ordering, and default linkage connectivity. Adding successor guidance or a standard representation/profile note would reduce migration ambiguity without restoring the whole old resource.

findingConsiderations.title: The full base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises many R4 resource REST endpoints
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: `SubstanceNucleicAcid` is included in this direct grouped endpoint finding. For this resource it should be handled together with the resource-removal decision: endpoint aliases would be expensive because they imply legacy model support, but CapabilityStatement or migration documentation should identify the replacement path so generic clients do not see only a silent disappearance.

findingConsiderations.title: Resource $meta-add is removed from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared Resource behavior can affect implementations broadly, but under the review instructions it is context only for `SubstanceNucleicAcid` and should be adjudicated at the `Resource` level rather than duplicated into this resource's migration score.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared Resource/DomainResource search metadata issue is relevant to global R4-to-R6 tooling migration but is not specific to the removed `SubstanceNucleicAcid` resource identity or its nucleic-acid content model.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Publish or confirm an authoritative R4 `SubstanceNucleicAcid` to R6 `SubstanceDefinition`/`Substance` migration map covering sequence type, subunit count/order, hybridisation, terminal residues, linkage connectivity, linkage/sugar identifiers, residue sites, and sequence attachments.

Add low-cost successor guidance for nucleic-acid representations in or around `SubstanceDefinition.structure`, including preservation of R4 5'-3' direction, default subunit count, subunit ordering, and default linkage assumptions.

Document the endpoint and generated-code transition explicitly: `SubstanceNucleicAcid` is not an R6 REST resource, and implementations should expose any legacy endpoint only as a compatibility feature with a stated mapping target.

Reconsider a deprecated transitional `SubstanceNucleicAcid` resource only if evidence emerges of substantial production, regulatory, or conformance dependence on the exact R4 resource shape; the current FMM 0/trial-use evidence does not by itself justify that cost.

caveats: The local inputs did not include an official cross-version ConceptMap, StructureMap, Jira rationale, or migration guide for the resource removal.
The inferred R6 successor is `SubstanceDefinition` and sometimes `Substance`; that inference should be checked against official HL7 migration guidance if available.
The R6 package reviewed is 6.0.0-ballot4, so final R6 content may differ.
Shared Resource and DomainResource behavior findings were considered as context only, per the review instructions.
